instruction: Design the main screen (a single page) for a Magic Academy learning game. Include an atmospheric academy hall or study scene, a student profile with rank and progress, a curriculum of magical course cards, a prominent current lesson, an upcoming exam panel, spell mastery indicators, and one clear Learn or Practice action. Put strong emphasis on an enchanting scholarly identity, readable progression, meaningful card differentiation, elegant typography, and polished visual craft.

history.critique: BRIEF/INTENT: The visible frame delivers the atmospheric hall (oculus + stained glass) and a complete profile, but the three most action-critical required elements are absent from view — the curriculum shows only its 'Paths of the Academy' heading with no course cards, there is no prominent current-lesson panel, no upcoming-exam panel, and no single Learn/Practice button anywhere in the viewport. The hero is spent on a decorative scene plus a full dashboard, so the player cannot tell what to do next; polish on the oculus does not excuse the missing CTA and lesson. CLARITY/HIERARCHY: Too many equal-weight focal points compete — the glowing oculus, the gold 72% bar, the gold '14', and four identically-styled stat tiles (XP / Curriculum / Spell Mastery / Rank) all pull the eye, so no single metric or action dominates. 'Spell mastery' is reduced to one 66% number, under-delivering the brief's plural 'indicators.' A real consistency bug: the header reads 'Apprentice' while the profile reads 'ADEPT II', contradicting the player's rank. VISUAL SYSTEM/CRAFT: The stained-glass columns are uniform hard-edged squares that read as a flat pixel mosaic, clashing with the otherwise refined letterpress/serif system; the left scene panel has no frame treatment while the right card has corner brackets (inconsistent framing language); a stray thin ellipse outline sits behind the caption text like an unfinished guide/stray shape; muted sub-labels ('to next rank: 1,520', 'top 11% this term') sit at low contrast on navy. EXPRESSIVENESS: The Meridian/celestial identity is coherent and the oculus is a genuine signature moment, but the composition is a generic two-column fantasy dashboard — the stat tiles are stock, and the scholarly character lives only in palette and type, not in the components themselves, so 'meaningful card differentiation' and an 'enchanting scholarly' feel are not yet realized in the UI objects.
history.suggestion: One prioritized plan that keeps all required content and the offline/HTML-only constraint: (1) REBUILD THE HERO FOR ACTION — make the Current Lesson the primary focal panel inside the first viewport, set against the oculus scene so atmosphere serves the task, with exactly one prominent gold CTA ('Continue Lesson' / 'Practice'); condense the profile to a compact strip (avatar, name, Adept II rank, 14-day streak, single 72% rank bar) and remove the 2x2 stat grid from the hero, folding XP/curriculum/rank into that strip or a secondary row. This resolves the missing-CTA, missing-lesson, and competing-focal-point problems at once. (2) COMPLETE THE REQUIRED MODULES in-viewport or immediately below with real differentiation: render the curriculum as course cards each coded by discipline (distinct hue + sigil icon + difficulty + progress ring + locked/active/done states); add a distinct Upcoming Exam panel styled as sealed parchment with date and prep progress; replace the single 66% with a dedicated Spell Mastery row of individual spell sigils carrying mastery pips/levels. (3) FIX CRAFT & CONSISTENCY — change the header rank to match the profile (Apprentice → Adept II); delete the stray ellipse behind the caption; apply one consistent frame language (corner brackets or hairline+corner ticks) to both the scene and profile panels; refine the stained glass with mullions/leading, gradient fills and varied tile geometry so it reads as glass; raise contrast on the muted sub-labels. (4) DEEPEN THE SCHOLARLY IDENTITY in the components, not just the palette — give the current lesson an illuminated-grimoire treatment (drop cap, gold rule, marginalia) and the exam a wax-seal motif, keeping the oculus as the signature moment but letting it sit behind the lesson so the enchanting identity is felt in every object the player actually uses.
